b.answer:
Worked example: a Harvest Lane test webhook that confirms which order it received.

#ModuleSettings
1Webhooks · Custom webhookName: HL test receiver. Run once, then send the sample below so Make learns the shape
2Webhooks · Webhook responseStatus: 200 · Body: the JSON below · Custom header: Content-Type = application/json

Response body in module 2:

{"received": true, "order_id": "{{1.order_id}}"}

Hoppscotch request: POST to the webhook URL, body type JSON:

{"order_id": "HL-0061"}

Reply shown in Hoppscotch: status 200, body {"received": true, "order_id": "HL-0061"}. Send it again with HL-0062 and the reply changes to match, which proves the value is mapped, not typed in.

Log: webhook trigger + response set up: yes. No keys or customer details needed.
mistakes: Typing "HL-0061" into the response body instead of mapping 1.order_id, so every reply is the same.
Not sending a sample request first, so Make doesn't know the order_id field.
Leaving the body as plain text without the Content-Type header, so Hoppscotch doesn't show it as JSON.
Sending the Hoppscotch body as form data instead of raw JSON, so order_id arrives empty.
b.pass: A Hoppscotch screenshot shows status 200 and the custom JSON reply containing the exact order_id that was sent, ideally for two different IDs.
b.redo: Send it back if the reply is Make's default reply rather than the custom JSON, or if the order_id is hard-coded.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's payment scenario in Paystack test mode with test keys stored in a keychain.

TestWhat I sentWhere it stoppedResult
Real paymentTest-card payment for HL-0061, ₦26,500Ran to the endOrder Paid, one receipt, data store record HL-0061-a1 (amount_kobo 2650000)
DuplicateResent the same webhook from HoppscotchExistence check (record exists)No second receipt; still one record
FakePOST with reference HL-FAKE-999Verify filter (Paystack: no successful transaction)Order unchanged
Wrong amountTest payment of ₦20,000 for HL-0062 (₦26,500 due)Amount check: 2000000 ≠ 2650000Tolu emailed "Partial or wrong payment for HL-0062"; status stays New
Other eventPOST event "transfer.success"Event filter after the responseNothing done

Data store after all tests: one record per real successful payment (HL-0061-a1). The partial payment isn't stored, so if it is resent, Tolu is alerted again rather than the order being marked Paid.

Every test returned 200 "ok" straight away, because the Webhook response sits right after the trigger. Credits: the duplicate, fake and other-event tests stopped early, so they used only a few credits each; check the figures in scenario history.

Outside Paystack's countries: the same five tests, with the HTTP module pointed at a webhook.site URL that returns a success JSON for the known reference only.

Submit: the table, a screenshot of the data store, and the scenario history list showing where each run stopped. Never include keys.
mistakes: Comparing Paystack's kobo amount with the naira total, so every payment is flagged as wrong.
Putting the existence check after the receipt, so duplicates still send a second receipt.
Typing the test secret key into a visible header instead of a keychain.
Using live keys or real customer details instead of test mode and sample data.
s.pass: All five tests are shown with where each run stopped (end, existence check, verify filter, amount check, event filter), and the data store holds exactly one record per real test payment.
s.redo: Send it back if any test is missing or stops in the wrong place, if a duplicate or fake produced a receipt, or if a key or live payment appears anywhere.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's holiday-aware 8 p.m. run.

Scenario A · HL · Holidays weekly (Mondays 06:00):

#ModuleSettings
1HTTP · Make a requestGET https://date.nager.at/api/v3/PublicHolidays/2026/NG (year from formatDate(now; "YYYY")); Parse response on
2Iteratorthe response body array
Link filterUpcoming onlydate ≥ today
3Data store · Add/replace a recordStore ng_holidays, key = date, field name

Changes to the 2.3 run:

#ModuleSettings
1 (new)Data store · Check the existence of a recordng_holidays, key = formatDate(addDays(now; 1); "YYYY-MM-DD")
2Sheets · Search Rowstomorrow's orders, as before; Not cancelled filter
3 (new)RouterHoliday route: exists = true · Normal route: exists = false
Holiday routeMessage + updateCustomer message: "Tomorrow is a public holiday, so your delivery moves to {{next working day}}." Then Update a Row: delivery_date = next working day (skip Sunday with the 2.2 d = 0 rule)
Normal routeThe 2.3 routerunchanged: rider list, reminder, big order, fallback
TestExpectedResult
Record "Test Holiday" added for tomorrow, 4 test orders4 moved messages, Deliveries tab empty4 messages, 0 rider rows ✓
Test record deleted, same ordersNormal routesRider list built ✓

Note for Tolu: back-to-back holidays (such as two-day Eid breaks) need the next-working-day check repeated; I flag those to Needs checking.

Submit: both scenarios, the data store contents, and the two test results.
mistakes: Calling the holiday API every night instead of weekly and storing the results.
Comparing tomorrow's date in a different format from the data store key (for example DD/MM/YYYY vs YYYY-MM-DD), so the check never matches.
Moving the delivery to a Sunday or to another holiday.
Testing only on a real holiday, or never testing at all, instead of adding a test record for tomorrow.
g.pass: The data store holds upcoming Nigerian holidays from the API; with a test holiday for tomorrow, the 8 p.m. run sends the "moved" messages and writes no rider list; with the record removed, it runs normally.
g.redo: Send it back if the rider list is still built on a holiday, if customers get no message, or if there's no evidence of the test holiday run.
